operator_io_quirks: Identifiers contain spaces and mixed case: "Customer ID", "Order Date", "Row ID", "Sub-Category"; all generated SQL must double-quote and double embedded quotes.
Composite PKs: people("Customer ID",Region), product("Product ID",Region); PK members are TEXT with distinct<rows (people 793<2501, product 1862<5298) so PK tuples repeat only via Region pairing.

Composite FKs: central/east/south/west_superstore have TWO FKs each sharing the Region column: ("Customer ID",Region)->people and ("Product ID",Region)->product. Region is a child column of two FKs simultaneously; upstream fks dict keyed by (child_t,child_c) will collide on Region (last wins) - must survive without crashing.

Region in each fact table has distinct=1 (Central/East/South/West) but the parent people/product Region has 4 values; FK draw from parent will produce cross-region values, breaking the intended partition - upstream does not care.

Declared type DATE on "Order Date"/"Ship Date" but storage class is text 'YYYY-MM-DD'; ts_fuzzer dispatch is 'Date|Number(int elements)' - first element '2013-01-03' does not parse as int so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d.
Postal Code declared INTEGER, storage integer, but semantically a 5-digit code (78664); Number fuzzer will produce arbitrary ints in [-10^0,10^0] scale 0 -> tiny values, not 5-digit.

Row ID INTEGER PK per fact table, distinct=rows, contiguous ranges per table (central 1..4646, east 4647.., south 10343.., west 13583..); Number fuzzer with scale 0 gives values in [-1,1] plus perturbation, so PK collisions are frequent and sample_fresh_primary_keys will drop most rows.
No NOT NULL anywhere (notnull=0 on every column), no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes; only PKs and FKs. Insert failures will be rare; row loss comes from PK/unique dedup, not constraints.
All null_rate=0.0 in original; TS Base drops None elements and p=1 if empty, so NULLs essentially never appear in generated instances.
Tables are small (2501..6406 rows) - no huge-table sampling concern; read_schema max_rows_per_table irrelevant here.

people.Customer ID distinct=793 but rows=2501: same customer appears in multiple regions; product.Product ID distinct=1862<5298 similarly. Parent PK is (ID,Region) so (ID,Region) is unique but ID alone is not.

Product Name samples contain commas and apostrophes ("O'Sullivan ...", trailing comma) - String fuzzer charset a-zA-Z 0-9() excludes both, so generated names lose punctuation; literal pool from train SQL may reintroduce them.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on Order Date/Ship Date: template %Y-%m-%d, range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (~2013-01..2014-12), so fresh dates stay in 2013-2014 window; plausible for date filters but no year-2011/2012 values unless in pool.

Number fuzzer on Row ID (INTEGER, scale 0): full range [-1,1] plus +-1/+-2 perturbation -> almost all rows collide on PK, sample_fresh_primary_keys keeps ~2-3 rows per fact table. Massive row loss -> many queries return empty or tiny results (FN risk on aggregates/counts).
Number fuzzer on Postal Code (INTEGER scale 0): values in {-2..2} roughly, never 5-digit; any query filtering Postal Code by real code returns empty (FN).

Number fuzzer on Sales/Profit/Discount (REAL, no args -> scale 0, precision 0): range [-1,1] plus +-0.01/+-0.02; Discount originals are 0.0-0.8 so plausible-ish, but Sales/Profit originals are 3..2573 -> generated values far too small (FN on Sales>X thresholds, FP on Profit<0 always true).
Number fuzzer on Quantity (INTEGER scale 0): values in {-2..2}+perturb, originals 1..14; queries Quantity>5 return empty (FN), Quantity>=1 mostly true (FP).

String fuzzer on Segment/Category/Ship Mode/Region (distinct 3-4): 5 original samples + pool literals, p=0.2 fresh random strings from a-zA-Z 0-9(); fresh draws are implausible ('x7Q(' etc.) -> equality filters on 'Consumer'/'Furniture' mostly hit pool values, but fresh contamination creates FP/FN on LIKE and != filters.

String fuzzer on Customer ID/Product ID/Order ID (structured codes like 'AA-10315','FUR-BO-10000112','CA-2011-103800'): fresh strings lose the code shape; LIKE 'CA-2011%' or 'FUR-%' filters will miss fresh values (FN) and match random strings rarely.

String fuzzer on Customer Name/City/State/Product Name: fresh random strings are not name-like; queries with LIKE '%a%' or State='Texas' rely on pool; pool from train SQL likely contains many real values so equality filters may still work.

FK fill: child Region drawn from parent people/product Region (4 values) with replacement, ignoring the per-table single-region semantics; joins on Region still work but partition queries (WHERE Region='Central' on central_superstore) will return rows with other regions (FP).

Composite FK collision: upstream fks dict keyed by (child_t,child_c) means Region maps to only one parent (people or product, last pragma wins); the other FK's ID column still draws from its parent but Region is drawn once - join on (Customer ID,Region) to people may fail to match (FN on join queries).

Row ID PK dedup happens AFTER FK draw; child fact tables draw Customer ID/Product ID from parent FINAL filtered columns (people/product PK dedup keeps ~most rows since 793/1862 distinct), so FK values are mostly valid but sparse.
Empty parent risk: if people/product PK dedup drops to few rows, fact tables draw from tiny parent sets -> heavy repetition of Customer ID/Product ID (FP on COUNT(DISTINCT)).
